base_member_text: [peakf,peakd]=find(Amp==v1) @L68 can return multiple cells for ties (subsequent scalar use assumes one); v1 from max(max(Amp)) @L67 while ind1 is unused
audit_member_text: Peak ties are not reduced to one location: find at L68 can return vector peakf/peakd, while colon ranges at L73-L74 require scalar endpoints; tied global maxima can therefore make truncation fail or become ambiguous (L67-L74).

base_member_text: Axis limits (0-8 S(f) @L39, 0-0.008 S(theta) @L47) and contour levels @L50 are dataset-specific; -71.8 deg rotation constant @L16 is FRF-array-specific and undocumented beyond the 'rotate 0 deg' comment; angle_end @L12, ind1, Hrms/Hrms_model computed but unused in output
audit_member_text: angle_end is assigned at L12 but never referenced through EOF L170; thmax instead derives solely from NumDir at L17, so changing angle_end has no effect on the direction grid (L12, L17-L19).

audit_member_text: The displayed phase is generated as Phase at L86 and plotted at L119, but the phase written to wave2d_frf.txt is independently regenerated as Phase_input at L137 and appended at L151; the phase panel therefore does not depict the output realization (L86, L119, L137, L151).

audit_member_text: The centered truncation formulas are inclusive at both ends: with an interior peak and even NFreq=50 or NDir=30 (L69-L72), L73-L74 select 51 or 31 indices respectively, exceeding the variables named as maxima by one.

The truncated frequency subplot plots x=Amp_Frq_model and y=Freq_model at L93, but L94-L95 label the y-axis as spectral density and x-axis as frequency, the reverse of both the plotted arguments and the corresponding raw subplot labels at L35-L37.

The 2-D amplitude is explicitly transposed to direction-by-frequency layout at L133-L136 before writing at L150, whereas the 1-D amplitude derived as a frequency-column vector at L159 is not transposed before L166 even though L162 declares NumDir=1; whether the consumer reads a flat stream or requires the same NumDir-by-NumFreq row layout is unresolved (L133-L136, L150, L159, L162, L166).

Each output remains open through fid after fprintf (L145-L149 and L161-L165) while dlmwrite separately appends to the same pathname before fclose (L150-L153 and L166-L168); ordering and buffering behavior for the two simultaneous file access paths is not established in this file.
